During his presidency (2009–2017), Barack Obama’s administration carried out military strikes—including drone attacks, airstrikes, and cruise missile launches—in at least seven countries, possibly eight, depending on definitions and sources. Here’s a breakdown:

⸻

🌍 Countries where Obama ordered military strikes
•Afghanistan
Continuation of the long-running war from the Bush era, with both manned aircraft and drones used in combat operations.  
•Iraq
Airstrikes began in August 2014 to combat ISIS and included both manned and unmanned aircraft.
•Pakistan
Numerous CIA drone strikes in tribal regions targeting militants—a major focus of Obama’s counterterror campaign.  
•Somalia
Drone and airstrikes against al‑Shabab militants; included special operations “signature” strikes.  
•Yemen
Extensive use of drones and some manned strikes targeting al‑Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula.
•Libya
Two campaigns: 2011 NATO-led airstrikes under UN mandate (“Odyssey Dawn/Unified Protector”) and later 2015–16 U.S. strikes against ISIS.
•Syria
Beginning in September 2014, Obama authorized airstrikes—including cruise missiles and drone use—against ISIS and other militant targets.  

⸻

🕵️‍♂️ Possible additional country
•Philippines
Some reports indicate U.S. drone strikes occurred in 2012 targeting militants—though this remains less confirmed. If included, this would raise the total to eight countries.
